reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator actively promotes paying from €30 to €5,000 for OneCoin packages presented as network activation and mining access, with tokens, daily points, commissions and payout claims as benefits. He further says the €5,000 package is probably the best value and emphasizes that company splits will double the tokens available for mining, encouraging viewers to purchase a paid mining package rather than merely reporting on it.

you'll be able to get a position with one coin
60,000 free tokens for mining here and the company does what they call splits so that's going to double the amount of tokens that you have to use for mining guys
this is probably going to be your best value between these two packages

opening.argument: Judge the recommendation for what it says, not as a guarantee. The speaker introduces the comparison as "In my opinion" and bases it on what he says he has researched (ASR_0002). Even his preference is qualified as "probably" the best value "between these two packages" (ASR_0002). That is a personal assessment of relative package value, not a stated promise that a buyer will earn a particular return. His claim about splits concerns the number of tokens available for mining (ASR_0002); it does not specify a cash payout from those tokens. The presentation is enthusiastic, but the quoted recommendation leaves the financial outcome unstated.

citations.quote: In my opinion guys from what I've researched and learned about this company
this is probably going to be your best value between these two packages
that's going to double the amount of tokens that you have to use for mining

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes prices, mining tokens and an expressed preference, but it treats a preference about value as though it promised a monetary result. The speaker's actual qualifier is "probably" (ASR_0002). Doubling tokens available "to use for mining" (ASR_0002) describes an allocation, not what those tokens will produce. Those distinctions matter when assessing whether this particular statement guarantees returns.

citations.quote: this is probably going to be your best value between these two packages
that's going to double the amount of tokens that you have to use for mining

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the recommendation an opinion does not undo the sales pitch. The speaker says the company "gonna pay you out" and refers to commissions (ASR_0001), then recommends value in the context of tokens for mining (ASR_0002). The defense is right that no exact cash return is specified, but a guaranteed figure is not necessary to see a paid package being promoted through claimed financial benefits.

opening.argument: This is a guided look at a package interface. The speaker calls the video an "educational tip" (ASR_0001), says he has been researching the company (ASR_0001), and introduces the screen as a back office where he will discuss packages (ASR_0001). He walks through tiers and their listed token and point quantities (ASR_0002; F0042). A viewer can understand that as a demonstration of what the interface presents, including his subjective comparison, without treating the screen's figures as verified earnings or his discussion as proof that mining will pay.

citations.quote: wanting to reach out with yet another educational tip on this company called one coin
where I've been actually doing some research on this company
so here we are in our back office here OneCoin and as we're going to talk about today excuse me packages

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes the €5,000 tier and the speaker's preference, but omits how he sets up the segment: "let's kind of dive right into it" to discuss packages (ASR_0001). Showing several tiers on the back-office screen (F0042) is consistent with a walkthrough. Neither a displayed Upgrade button nor a comparison, on its own, demonstrates that a viewer purchased anything or received a return.

citations.quote: but what we kind of want to talk about today guys were just packages so let's kind of dive right into it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough framing does not account for the endorsement within it. The speaker says "this company is true" (ASR_0001), calls the expensive packages the probable best value (ASR_0002), and points to tokens for mining as the reason (ASR_0002). The defense shows that the interface is demonstrated, but not that the discussion is neutral instruction rather than promotion of paid mining access.

citations.quote: this company is true
this is probably going to be your best value between these two packages
60,000 free tokens for mining here

opening.argument: The material can be read as a comparison of priced packages, not evidence that any buyer receives a fraudulent return. The speaker describes the €30 activation as an entry into the network (ASR_0001), while the interface shows packages with prices, included quantities and Upgrade buttons (F0023; F0042). The €1,000 tier is described in terms of tokens, gold coins, business volume and daily points (ASR_0002). Those are listed package contents; the cited material does not show a completed payment, a buyer's realized earnings, or a fixed cash return. The judge should distinguish promotion of a package from proof of the further financial outcome alleged to follow from buying it.

citations.quote: you'll be able to get a position with one coin with a simple activation fee here 30 euros
this package is a thousand euros but it comes with 10,000 free tokens so you have ten thousand tokens to mine with

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies paid tiers, but a price beside token quantities is not itself evidence of realized returns. Even the speaker's split claim is about doubling "the amount of tokens" (ASR_0002), not doubling money. The interface presents a catalog with different prices and listed inclusions (F0042). The prosecution's account relies on treating the promoted mining-related contents as an established payout mechanism.

citations.quote: that's going to double the amount of tokens that you have to use for mining

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is what the video promotes, not whether a purchase or payout is captured on screen. The speaker ties a €1,000 price directly to tokens "to mine with" (ASR_0002), recommends the €5,000 package based on its mining tokens (ASR_0002), and claims the company pays commissions (ASR_0001). Describing those as catalog entries does not remove the paid mining and financial-benefit pitch.
